newsitem.title: IRAN: Pakistan minister discusses Afghan crisis in Iran.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan minister discusses Afghan crisis in Iran.

text.p: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Sahibzada Yaqoob Khan arrived in Tehran on Wednesday to try to coordinate policy towards Afghanistan with Iranian leaders.

State-run Tehran radio said Khan met Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and told him the two countries should continue their efforts and consultations aimed at ending the crisis in neighbouring Afghanistan.
Velayati said the exchanges of views were "a good start for renewed cooperation between the two countries in this area".
He also expressed support for U.N.-sponsored peace talks between rival Afghan factions which started on Monday in Islamabad, the radio added.
Iran and Pakistan hold contrasting views of the Taleban Islamic movement, which seized Kabul in September, but have sought to contain their differences by maintaining a dialogue on Afghanistan.
Khan is scheduled to also meet Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri during his three-day visit.
Iran has charged Pakistan with setting up and supporting the Taleban, saying the group also is backed by the United States. Pakistan denies favouring any faction.
Tehran recognises the government of ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani but it has urged Afghan factions to reach a power-sharing agreement.
"We in Iran expect him (Khan) to clear the air and declare Pakistan's official Afghan policy," the daily Iran News said on Wednesday in an editorial commentary.

"Taleban not only deprived several ethnic communities of that country of their fundamental rights but also misrepresented true Islam through whimsical interpretations of this great religion," the English-language newspaper said.
